text.p: The following are the main stories in Slovenia's Friday morning newspapers:
- The coalition parties have not yet agreed the 1997 budget proposal.
- The controlling board of trading firm Mercator decided to change its management following a suggestion by five board members representing employees.
- Parliament has decided to prohibit the return of forests and land nationalised after the second world war until December 20 as it waits for more detailed legislation on the subject.
- The Ministry of Education said it would subsidise rents in private appartments for 800 students.
- Telecommunications firm Digitel said it had applied for permission to operate a mobile phone network.
- The number of registered unemployed rose to 122,613 in June from 113,000 in the same month last year, the Statistical Office said.
- Parliament is expected to debate a bill on partial privatisation of Slovenian Ironworks soon.
- In the first half of 1997 government spending reached 23.8 billion tolars less than 354.7 billion planned in the draft budget for the first six months of the year.
